You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` attempts to override the geometric mean implementation in the `SummaryStatistics` class using `setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean())`. The test then adds values and checks that the geometric mean result matches the expected value computed by a standalone `GeometricMean` object.

From the code snippets:
- `setGeoMeanImpl()` calls `checkEmpty()` which throws an exception if any values have been added before the override.
- `addValue(double)` increments all statistics including `geoMeanImpl` only if the current implementation differs from the default `GeometricMean` class.
- `getGeometricMean()` returns `geoMeanImpl.getResult()`, which is the stored computed result.

The current bug report is about a different statistic: after setting a new variance implementation in `setVarianceImpl()`, `getStandardDeviation()` returns NaN. Investigating reveals:
- `setVarianceImpl()` also calls `checkEmpty()` to prevent resetting varianceImpl after data has been added.
- `getStandardDeviation()` computes the square root of `getVariance()` (which returns `varianceImpl.getResult()`), but it can return NaN if varianceImpl contains no valid data.
- `addValue()` increments variance only if the current variance implementation is not the default `Variance` class.

Combining these insights:
- Both the geometric mean and variance implementations can be replaced only before any data is added, enforced by `checkEmpty()`.
- When a new statistic implementation is set (e.g., a new GeometricMean or Variance), it must be fresh and ready to accumulate data.
- The bug report suggests `setVarianceImpl(new Variance(false))` (a new variance implementation) leads to `NaN` standard deviation, which likely means varianceImpl was replaced after data was added or replaced but never accumulated new data.
- The test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` works because it sets the new geoMeanImpl before adding any data, and the new implementation is updated with values in `addValue`.

Therefore, the observed bug is probably caused by invoking `setVarianceImpl()` after values have already been added (which `checkEmpty()` prevents and throws), or by replacing the variance implementation before adding data but neglecting to ensure it accumulates values properly. Alternatively, if `setVarianceImpl()` is called when no data has been added, then `getStandardDeviation()` returns NaN because varianceImpl's `getResult()` returns NaN as no values have been accumulated yet. The user might call `getStandardDeviation()` prematurely before adding values.

In sum, the root cause for NaN is that the variance implementation is replaced but no values are yet fed to it, so the stored result is NaN. This is consistent with the `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` test behavior which correctly replaces the geometric mean implementation before data accrual, so the statistical results are correctly computed.

No relevant recent bug reports relate directly to stats impl replacement or NaN return for standard deviation or geometric mean, so this is an isolated design/usage issue.

# Summary:
- Both `setGeoMeanImpl()` and `setVarianceImpl()` enforce being called only before data is added (`checkEmpty()`).
- The new statistic impls must accumulate data after being set and before querying result.
- `getStandardDeviation()` returns NaN if variance impl has no data.
- The failing test correctly sets geoMeanImpl before adding data and works as expected.
- The reported bug arises because `setVarianceImpl()` is called but variance impl has no data before invoking `getStandardDeviation()`, resulting in NaN.

Recommended fix: Add usage or documentation clarity that these impl setters must be called before adding values, and that querying statistics before adding values may yield NaN for some statistics. Also, verify that `checkEmpty()` is indeed preventing illegal usage.

The root error is consistent with the class design and test usage pattern.

The best methods to fix or clarify this are likely the setters:
- `SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic)`
- `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic)`
and possibly `SummaryStatistics.getStandardDeviation()` to handle no-data cases more gracefully.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
